Ok. We get there, get a hoseline to the front door, charge it up and make entry. When we get inside, we know where she will be. We know she's not moving. We know we can't move her. Big people breathe down airpacks fast, so there will be some swapping of airpacks, so someone will be going in and out of the building throughout the entire opertation. It makes the fight more dangerous, harder to win, and creates more work while simultaneously removing at least one, but probably two people from the fire supression operation.

tl;dr: Obese victims are too heavy to remove from the fire, so we have to fight the fire around them, then establish patient care inside a working fire, creating more work, occupying the skills of much needed personnel, and then creating more work again after the fire, when we're all exhausted.
